questions.q: What are the three steps of the idea behind groupby?
options: Split into groups, apply a function, combine the results
questions.explain: groupby splits rows into groups, applies a function such as sum or mean to each group, and combines the outputs into one table.

questions.q: A group has one row whose amount is missing. What do groupby(...).size() and groupby(...)["amount"].count() return for that group?
questions.explain: size counts rows in the group, including rows with missing values. count counts only non-missing values in the chosen column.

questions.q: Which call produces a customer summary with columns named n_orders and total?
questions.explain: Named aggregation uses new_name=(column, function) keyword arguments inside agg.

questions.q: You want each order's share of its customer's total spend, keeping all original rows. Which groupby method fits?
options: agg, because it shrinks the table to one row per customer
size, because it counts the rows
filter, because it drops small groups
transform, because it returns a result aligned to every original row
questions.explain: transform returns a value for every original row, so you can divide each amount by its group's total. It is like SUM() OVER (PARTITION BY ...) in SQL.

questions.q: A group contains only missing amounts. What does groupby(...)["amount"].sum() return for it?
options: 0, which can be mistaken for real data
The group is removed from the result
questions.explain: sum skips missing values, so an all-missing group sums to 0. mean, by contrast, returns NaN. Check counts alongside sums.
